questions.question: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?

options.A: A programming language used to write software
options.B: A field that builds systems to simulate or extend human intelligence in real-world tasks
options.C: A database management system
options.D: A hardware device for fast computing

questions.question: Which of the following best defines Machine Learning?

options.A: Hard-coding rules into a system manually
options.B: Algorithms that learn from data to improve performance without explicit programming
options.C: A type of database query language
options.D: A networking protocol for AI systems

questions.question: Deep Learning is best described as:

options.A: A subset of ML that uses rule-based systems
options.B: A completely separate field from Machine Learning
options.C: A subset of ML that uses multi-layer neural networks to learn rich representations from raw data

questions.question: Which three core elements drive AI development?

options.A: Rules, Experts, and Databases
options.B: Computing Power, Data, and Algorithms
options.C: Hardware, Internet, and Cloud

questions.question: What is the role of 'Data' in AI development?

options.A: The engine of AI

questions.question: What is the role of 'Algorithms' in AI development?

options.A: The fuel of AI
options.B: The brain and command center of AI

options.A: Chatbots and customer support

options.A: Bounding boxes around objects
options.B: A pixel-level map partitioning the image into multiple segments

options.A: Rule-based grammar systems only

options.A: Email spam detection

options.A: Translating text from one language to another
options.B: Detecting objects in an image for further processing with intelligent algorithms

options.A: Always improve as more data is added
options.B: Saturate with more data and struggle with high-dimensional raw data
options.C: Decrease with more data
options.D: Be unaffected by the amount of training data

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of classical ML mentioned in the course?

options.A: Limited representation capacity
options.B: Struggles with high-dimensional raw data like images and audio

questions.question: The course covers which deep learning architectures?

options.A: CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers only

questions.question: How is Machine Learning defined according to Tom Mitchell's classic definition?

options.A: A program that follows explicit rules to solve problems
options.B: A program that learns from experience E with respect to task T and improves performance P
options.C: A system that only works with numerical data

questions.question: In the ML pipeline, what comes BEFORE model training?

options.A: Model deployment
options.B: Model evaluation
options.C: Data preparation, cleansing, and feature selection

questions.question: What is the 'curse of dimensionality'?

options.A: The problem of having too few training samples
options.B: What happens when you have too many features compared to the amount of data
options.C: Overfitting caused by deep neural networks
options.D: The inability of a model to generalize

questions.question: Which type of ML uses labeled data with known correct outputs?

options.A: Unsupervised Learning
options.B: Reinforcement Learning
options.C: Supervised Learning

questions.question: In Supervised Learning, the model improves by:

options.A: Exploring the environment and receiving rewards
options.B: Clustering similar data points together
options.C: Comparing its predictions with correct labels and adjusting
options.D: Using unlabeled data to find hidden patterns

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a Classification task?

options.A: Predicting tomorrow's temperature
options.B: Estimating next week's stock price
options.C: Deciding whether an email is spam or not

questions.question: Regression is used to predict:

options.A: A category or class label
options.B: Continuous numerical values
options.C: Cluster assignments

questions.question: Unsupervised Learning works with:

options.A: Labeled data with correct answers
options.B: Unlabeled data; no correct answers are given
options.C: Data collected from environment interactions

questions.question: In Reinforcement Learning, the agent learns by:

options.A: Comparing its output to labeled data
options.B: Grouping similar data points
options.C: Interacting with the environment to maximize cumulative reward

questions.question: What is 'Overfitting' in machine learning?

options.A: The training error is large, meaning the model is too simple
options.B: The model performs well on training data but has large generalization error on new data
options.C: The model has equal training and test error
options.D: The model is trained on too little data

questions.question: What is 'Underfitting'?

options.A: The training error is small but generalization error is large
options.B: The training error itself is large (model is too simple to capture the pattern)
options.C: The model has too many parameters

questions.question: What does 'Generalization' mean in ML?

options.A: How well the model performs on training data
options.B: The accuracy of predictions based on new, unseen data
options.C: The number of parameters in the model

questions.question: The Filter method for feature selection:

options.A: Uses a prediction model to score feature subsets
options.B: Evaluates each feature independently based on its correlation with the target variable
options.C: Treats feature selection as part of the modeling process
options.D: Combines benefits of wrapper and embedded methods

questions.question: The Wrapper method for feature selection:

options.A: Evaluates features independently without using a model
options.B: Uses different combinations of features scored by a prediction model
options.C: Is the same as the Filter method

questions.question: Which feature selection method combines the benefits of both Filter and Wrapper methods?

options.A: Filter method
options.B: Wrapper method
options.C: Embedded method

questions.question: What are the three common types of problems in dirty data?

options.A: Missing, Duplicate, and Sorted data
options.B: Incompleteness, Noise, and Inconsistency
options.C: Overfitting, Underfitting, and Bias

questions.question: A 'Training Set' is used for:

options.A: Evaluating the final generalization of the model
options.B: Tuning hyperparameters only
options.C: Building (learning) the model from data

questions.question: A 'Test Set' is used for:

options.A: Training the model weights
options.B: Validating hyperparameter choices
options.C: Evaluating the learned model's generalization capability

questions.question: Why is Data Standardization important?

options.A: To increase the number of features in the dataset
options.B: To reduce noise and improve model accuracy by putting features on comparable scales
options.C: To remove all outliers from the dataset
options.D: To convert categorical features into numerical ones

questions.question: When should Machine Learning be preferred over rule-based systems?

options.A: When rules are simple and fixed
options.B: When the problem is well-understood with stable rules
options.C: When rules are complex, tasks change over time, or data distributions shift
options.D: When the dataset is very small

lecture: Lecture 3 – Linear Regression and Decision Trees

questions.question: What is a Model Parameter?

options.A: A configuration set by the user before training
options.B: A value learned from data that defines the model's function and is saved as part of the model
options.C: The number of training epochs

questions.question: Which of the following is a Model Hyperparameter?

options.A: The weights of a neural network
options.B: The bias terms in linear regression
options.C: The learning rate and number of neurons in a neural network

questions.question: In k-fold Cross-Validation, the dataset is:

options.A: Split into two halves: training and testing
options.B: Split into K equal parts, each used once as the test set while training on the remaining K-1 parts
options.C: Used entirely for training with a separate validation set
options.D: Randomly shuffled K times without any structured splitting

questions.question: What is the main benefit of k-fold Cross-Validation?

options.A: It increases the size of the training dataset
options.B: It provides a more reliable and stable estimate of model performance
options.C: It eliminates the need for a test set entirely

questions.question: Linear Regression assumes:

options.A: A non-linear relationship between input and output
options.B: A linear relationship between input (independent variable) and output (dependent variable)
options.C: Outputs must be binary (0 or 1)
options.D: All input features must be categorical

questions.question: In the equation y = b0 + b1*x, what does b1 represent?

options.A: The intercept of the regression line
options.B: The dependent variable
options.C: The slope (coefficient) that relates the input x to the output y

questions.question: What is a 'residual' in Linear Regression?

options.A: The slope of the regression line
options.B: The distance between the observed value and the value predicted by the regression line
options.C: The average of all predictions
options.D: The number of data points used in training

questions.question: The Least Squares method minimizes:

options.A: The sum of absolute differences between actual and predicted values
options.B: The maximum single prediction error
options.C: The sum of squared differences (residuals) between actual and predicted values
options.D: The total number of misclassified samples

questions.question: Mean Squared Error (MSE) is calculated as:

options.A: The sum of all residuals
options.B: The maximum residual value
options.C: (1/n) × Σ(predicted – actual)²
options.D: The square root of the sum of residuals

questions.question: Which of the following is a real-world application of Linear Regression?

options.A: Classifying emails as spam or not spam
options.B: Predicting salary based on years of experience
options.C: Clustering customers into groups

questions.question: In a Decision Tree, the 'Root Node' is:

options.A: Any node that makes a final prediction
options.B: A node with no children at the bottom of the tree
options.C: The top node representing the full dataset and the first split
options.D: A node that performs no splitting

questions.question: What is a 'Leaf Node' in a Decision Tree?

options.A: The first node at the top of the tree
options.B: An internal node that performs a split
options.C: A terminal node that makes the final prediction (no further splits)
options.D: A node with exactly two children

questions.question: How does a Decision Tree choose which feature to split on?

options.A: It always splits on the first feature in the dataset
options.B: It splits on the feature that results in the lowest Gini Impurity (most pure split)
options.C: It randomly selects a feature at each node
options.D: It splits based on the highest feature value

questions.question: What does a Gini Impurity value of 0 mean?

options.A: The node is maximally impure with equal class distribution
options.B: The node is pure — all samples belong to one class
options.C: The node needs to be split further
options.D: The feature was not useful for splitting

questions.question: What is the maximum Gini Impurity value for a binary classification problem?
Which of the following are valid Decision Tree splitting criteria mentioned in the lecture?

options.A: MSE, MAE, and RMSE
options.B: Gini Index, Information Gain, and Gain Ratio
options.C: Precision, Recall, and F1-Score

questions.question: A Decision Tree stops splitting when:

options.A: The tree reaches exactly 10 nodes
options.B: A node is pure, no features remain, or a stopping condition (e.g., max depth) is met
options.C: The training accuracy reaches 100%

questions.question: Decision Trees are described as 'upside down' because:

options.A: Predictions flow from leaves to root
options.B: The root node is at the top and leaves are at the bottom
options.C: They are read from right to left
options.D: The deepest node is the most important

questions.question: The goal of each split in a Decision Tree is to:

options.A: Maximize the number of nodes
options.B: Minimize the depth of the tree
options.C: Un-mix the data or reduce uncertainty at each node
options.D: Increase the Gini Impurity of child nodes

questions.question: Which variable is called the 'dependent variable' in Linear Regression?

options.A: X — the input feature used for prediction
options.B: b0 — the intercept
options.C: Y — the output variable being predicted

lecture: Lecture 4 – Random Forest and Ensemble Learning

questions.question: What is the core idea of a Random Forest algorithm?

options.A: Using a single very deep decision tree
options.B: Using many decision trees, each trained on random data/features, with combined results
options.C: Applying gradient descent to decision tree nodes
options.D: Training one tree on the full dataset multiple times

questions.question: How does Random Forest combine tree predictions for classification?

options.A: Averaging the probability outputs of all trees
options.B: Taking the prediction of the best-performing single tree
options.C: Majority voting across all trees

questions.question: How does Random Forest combine tree predictions for regression?

options.A: Majority voting
options.B: Averaging predictions across all trees
options.C: Using the median prediction

questions.question: What is 'Bootstrapping' in Random Forests?

options.A: Pruning trees to reduce their depth
options.B: Taking random samples WITH replacement from the training data to create new datasets
options.C: Applying regularization to each tree
options.D: Normalizing the feature values before training

questions.question: What makes Random Forest different from a single Decision Tree?

options.A: Random Forest uses Gini Impurity while Decision Trees do not
options.B: Random Forest introduces randomness by using random subsets of data and features for each tree
options.C: Random Forest is always less accurate than a single tree
options.D: Random Forest only works for regression problems

questions.question: Which assumption of Random Forest states that results are more reliable with sufficient training data?

options.A: Each tree makes its own decisions
options.B: Random parts of the data are used
options.C: Enough data is needed
options.D: All trees must agree on predictions

questions.question: Ensemble Learning solves the problem of a single model by:

options.A: Using more training data than a single model
options.B: Aggregating multiple models and balancing their errors
options.C: Training one model for a longer time

questions.question: Which ensemble method trains models independently IN PARALLEL?

options.A: Boosting
options.B: Stacking's meta-learner phase
options.C: Bagging

questions.question: Which ensemble method trains models SEQUENTIALLY, each correcting the previous?

options.A: Bagging
options.B: Random Forest
options.C: Boosting

questions.question: What is the main goal of Bagging?

options.A: Reduce bias
options.B: Reduce variance and prevent overfitting
options.C: Improve generalization through a meta-learner

questions.question: What is the main goal of Boosting?

options.A: Reduce variance
options.B: Reduce bias and turn weak learners into strong ones
options.C: Use entirely different model types

questions.question: In Boosting, after each iteration, misclassified samples receive:

options.A: Lower weights so they are less likely to be selected
options.B: The same weight as before
options.C: Higher weights so subsequent models focus on them
options.D: Zero weight to be excluded from training

questions.question: Stacking combines predictions using:

options.A: Simple majority voting
options.B: Averaging all model predictions
options.C: A meta-learner (second-level model) trained on base model outputs
options.D: Weighted voting based on model depth

questions.question: In Stacking, what type of models are typically used as base models?

options.A: Only decision trees
options.B: Only neural networks
options.C: Different types of models (e.g., Trees, SVMs, KNN)

questions.question: What type of model is commonly used as the meta-learner in Stacking?

options.A: A deep neural network
options.B: Logistic Regression
options.C: A Random Forest

questions.question: Which ensemble method uses the ENTIRE dataset but re-weights samples after each round?

options.A: Bagging
options.B: Stacking
options.C: Random Forest

questions.question: Can Bagging models be trained in parallel?

options.A: No — they must be sequential like Boosting
options.B: Yes — base models are trained independently so parallel training is possible
options.C: Only when using neural networks as base models
options.D: Only when the dataset is very large

questions.question: Which of the following algorithms is an example of a Boosting method?

options.A: Random Forest
options.B: Bagged Trees
options.C: AdaBoost and Gradient Boosting

questions.question: Why do ensembles generally work better than single models?

options.A: They use more complex loss functions
options.B: They require more computational resources which improves accuracy
options.C: Multiple models with different errors cancel each other out, reducing overall error
options.D: They always use larger datasets than single models

questions.question: In the Ensemble Models Summary, which method uses 'weighted sum based on model accuracy' for combination?

options.A: Bagging
options.B: Stacking
options.C: Boosting

questions.question: Neural Networks are described as computational models inspired by:

options.A: The structure of computer processors
options.B: How the human brain learns
options.C: Database management systems

options.C: Bootstrap samples and meta-learners
options.D: Training sets and test sets only

questions.question: What are 'Weights and Biases' in a Neural Network?

options.A: Fixed constants set by the data scientist
options.B: Adjustable parameters that determine how strongly inputs affect a neuron
options.C: The output values of the network
options.D: The activation functions applied at each layer

questions.question: The neural network training loop is:

options.A: Data → Features → Model → Prediction

questions.question: The Output Layer activation function for multi-class classification should be:

options.B: To initialize weights to zero

questions.question: What happens if all layers use only Linear Activation Functions?

questions.question: How does ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) function work?

options.A: The vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs

questions.question: The Softmax function is used to:

options.A: Introduce non-linearity in hidden layers
options.B: Replace ReLU in convolutional layers
options.C: Transform output scores into a probability distribution summing to 1

questions.question: According to the activation function comparison table, which function is used in 'Most hidden layers'?

options.A: Sigmoid
options.B: Tanh
options.C: ReLU

questions.question: Leaky ReLU differs from ReLU in that:

options.A: It outputs 1 for all positive values

options.C: It is used only in the output layer
options.D: It has an output range of (0, 1)

questions.question: Which activation function gives 'much higher probability to the largest input value, while pushing all others closer to zero'?

options.A: ReLU
options.B: Sigmoid
options.C: Tanh

questions.question: The 'Learning Rule' in a neural network refers to:

options.A: The choice of optimizer algorithm only

questions.question: A Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) must have AT LEAST how many layers?

options.A: One layer (input only)
options.B: Two layers (input and output)
options.C: Three layers (input, hidden, output)

options.A: Information flows both forward and backward during prediction

options.C: Feedback loops exist between layers during inference

questions.question: Why can a Single-Layer Perceptron NOT solve the XOR problem?

options.A: It does not have enough neurons
options.B: It cannot handle more than two features

In Forward Propagation, the computation at each neuron is:

options.A: Subtract inputs from weights and apply activation

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Loss Function in a neural network?

options.A: To decide the architecture of the network
options.B: To measure how far the model's prediction is from the true label

questions.question: Cross-Entropy Loss is most appropriate for:

options.A: Regression problems predicting continuous values
options.B: Clustering problems

options.A: Multi-class classification
options.B: Binary classification
options.C: Regression tasks predicting continuous values

questions.question: In Backpropagation, the error is propagated:

options.A: From input to output, same direction as forward pass

options.C: From output back through the network layer by layer

questions.question: What do gradients in backpropagation tell us?

options.B: How much each weight contributed to the error and the direction to reduce it

options.D: Which features to remove from the dataset

questions.question: Weights are updated in the direction that:

options.A: Increases the loss function
options.B: Is opposite to the gradient (reduces the error)
options.C: Maintains the current gradient value

questions.question: The Learning Rate controls:

options.A: The number of hidden layers in the network

questions.question: The formula MSE = (1/n) × Σ(predicted – actual)² measures:

options.C: The total absolute error across all predictions

questions.question: In backpropagation, calculating gradients requires:

questions.question: Which statement about the MLP is TRUE?

options.A: MLP requires at least two hidden layers to function

questions.question: Why is MLP not suitable for image classification on large images?

options.A: MLP cannot use ReLU activation functions
options.B: MLP ignores spatial relationships between pixels and causes a massive parameter explosion
options.C: MLP only handles grayscale images, not color images

questions.question: For a 224×224×3 color image processed by an MLP, how many input neurons are required?
CNN addresses MLP's weakness through which three key concepts?

options.A: Softmax, Cross-Entropy, and Gradient Descent

options.C: Pooling, Flattening, and Fully-Connected Layers

questions.question: What is 'Local Connectivity' in CNNs?

options.A: Each neuron connects to all pixels in the entire image
options.B: Each neuron is connected only to a small local region of the input
options.C: Neurons are connected only to neurons in the next layer, not the previous
options.D: All neurons share the same activation function

questions.question: What is 'Parameter Sharing' in CNNs?

options.B: The same filter/kernel (set of weights) is used across all spatial locations of the image
options.C: Parameters are shared between different network architectures
options.D: Weights are shared between the encoder and decoder

questions.question: What does the Convolution operation produce?

options.A: A probability distribution over classes
options.B: A 1D vector ready for classification
options.C: A Feature Map showing where a particular pattern was detected in the input
options.D: A normalized version of the input image

questions.question: In a Feature Map, high values indicate:

options.A: The filter did not match the pattern at that location
options.B: The location has zero activation
options.C: A strong match between the filter and the input at that location
options.D: The pooling operation reduced that region

questions.question: What activation function is most commonly applied after convolution in CNNs?

options.A: Sigmoid
options.B: Tanh
options.C: Softmax

questions.question: ReLU in CNNs keeps positive values and:

options.A: Doubles all positive values
options.B: Replaces negative values with zero
options.C: Normalizes all values to the range (0, 1)

questions.question: What does 'Stride' control in a CNN?
